title: What does a range total cost?
hook: Eight days of sales, running totals ready. How much reading to total days 3 to 7?

doesNotKnow: that one pass of running totals lets you total any stretch of the list with a single subtraction
that the cost is paid when a number changes

misconception: Totalling a stretch of a list always means adding every number in it, so longer stretches always take longer.
objective: The learner can explain that after one pass of running totals (7 additions for 8 days) the total of days l to r is the running total at r minus the running total at l - 1 (days 3 to 7: 25 - 4 = 21), so any range costs two reads and one subtraction however long, and that changing one day makes every later running total stale.

claims.text: The running totals of 3 1 4 1 5 9 2 6 are 3, 4, 8, 9, 14, 23, 25, 31 (each new total = the total to its left + the day above).
claims.source: Arithmetic; builder re-ran in node 2026-10-14. Demo.tsx prefix() computes the row the stage shows. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own node: running totals of 3 1 4 1 5 9 2 6 are 3, 4, 8, 9, 14, 23, 25, 31; Demo prefix() and 'Next total' (truth[built.length]) produce the same row.

claims.text: The total of days l to r equals the running total at r minus the running total at l - 1; days 3 to 7 give 25 - 4 = 21, the same as 4 + 1 + 5 + 9 + 2. The total up to day 7 already holds days 1 and 2, so subtracting the total up to day 2 leaves the range.
claims.source: The sum to r is the sum to l - 1 plus the range. Builder's node check 2026-10-14: all 36 ranges l..r of the 8 days match P[r] - P[l-1] (P0 = 0). | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own node: all 36 ranges l..r equal P[r] − P[l−1] (P0 = 0); days 3-7: 25 − 4 = 21 = 4 + 1 + 5 + 9 + 2. Paths: checkRange records only from a complete, non-stale row; if the learner presses 'Day 3 + 1' before building, the reveal quotes the edited values (26 − 4 = 22 = 5 + 1 + 5 + 9 + 2), still true and on the trace line. Reset does not clear qSeen.

claims.text: Building the 8 running totals takes 7 additions, once; after that any range costs two reads and one subtraction, however long.
claims.source: The first total copies day 1; each of the other 7 is one addition. A range l..r reads P[r] and P[l-1] and subtracts. Edge case: a range starting at day 1 needs only P[r] (1 read, no subtraction); the stage shows 'reads 1' for it. Fact-checker: judge whether 'any range costs one subtraction' needs 'at most'. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): DISPUTED. The arithmetic of building holds (7 additions; adds is always N − 1). But 'after that any range costs two reads and one subtraction' is not true of every range, and the stage shows the exception: a range starting at day 1 reads one total and subtracts nothing (readout 'Days 1–6: total 23 · reads 1 · adding: 6 numbers'). The stage opens at from 1, to 6, so this is the first range the learner sees. 8 of the 36 ranges start at day 1. The reveal repeats it: 'Any range costs one subtraction, however long.' Fix (builder; owner decides wording): 'at most two reads and one subtraction' in the claim and reveal, or define the zero total P0 on the stage so day-1 ranges also read two cells. Blocks publishing.

claims.text: Adding 1 to day 3 makes the running totals of days 3 to 8 stale (6 of 8); that is the price of the fast ranges.
claims.source: Every running total from day 3 on includes day 3. Builder's node check 2026-10-14: 6 of 8 totals change. Demo.tsx counts built totals that differ from prefix(current values). | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own node: adding 1 to day 3 changes totals 3..8, 6 of 8. Traced every order: edit before build, edit mid-build (row mixes old and new totals) and repeated edits always count 6 stale against the new truth (built totals from day 3 on are always from a smaller day-3 value). staleSeen is recorded only from a complete row; the reveal prints it.

recall.question: Running totals of a list of 1,000 numbers are ready. How many of them do you need to total items 200 to 900?
recall.why: The running totals at 900 and at 199: their difference is the total of items 200 to 900, however long the range.
